subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
unit: Unit 4: Service With a Smile (Listening & Speaking)
lesson: Listening 3.4.3 and Soundbites: complaining and responding to complaints
outcomes: Identify a hotel guest's complaints and the receptionist's promises
Use polite phrases to complain and respond to complaints
Discuss solutions to problems and the idea 'The customer is always right'

tf.s: The guest complains that his room has no sea view.
tf.why: His room looks over the car park instead of the sea.

tf.s: The guest is happy with the towels in his room.
tf.why: He complains that the towels are dirty.

tf.s: The receptionist promises to call the maintenance department about the air conditioning.
tf.why: Maintenance fixes broken things like air conditioners.

tf.s: 'I can only apologise' is a phrase for complaining.
tf.why: It is a phrase for responding to a complaint.

tf.s: 'It's just not up to standard' is a phrase for complaining.
tf.why: It says that something is not good enough.

tf.s: The guest says the hotel is supposed to be five-star but feels more like a two-star hotel.
tf.why: That is why he is so disappointed.

tf.s: The phrase 'The customer is always right' was coined by Harry Gordon Selfridge.
tf.why: He was the founder of Selfridge's.

tf.s: One criticism of 'The customer is always right' is that some customers can be rude.
tf.why: Staff may be unhappy when a rude customer is wrong.

tf.s: Intonation does not matter when you complain or apologise.
tf.why: The right intonation helps you sound polite and sincere.

tf.s: The guest's sandwich from room service was exactly what he ordered.

boxes.q: What did the guest's window look over?
boxes.why: He wanted a sea view but saw the car park.

boxes.q: What was wrong with the towels?
boxes.why: The guest complains about dirty towels.

boxes.q: What was wrong with the food from room service?
boxes.why: He got a sandwich he did not order.

boxes.q: Which department will fix the air conditioning?
Which phrase responds to a complaint?
o: I'm not very happy about it.
I've got a complaint about my room.

boxes.q: Who coined 'The customer is always right'?

boxes.why: To apologise is to say you are sorry.

boxes.q: Which phrase introduces a hypothetical solution?
o: The best idea would be to...

boxes.q: How many stars did the guest say the hotel felt like?
boxes.why: It should be five-star but felt like two-star.

hunt.q: Who will fix the air conditioning?
The hotel felt like a ...-star hotel
Not good enough: not up to ...

mcq.q: What does the guest complain about?
o: No sea view, dirty towels, a faulty air conditioner and the wrong sandwich
The price of the room only
The noise from the swimming pool
mcq.why: These are the four problems in the listening.

mcq.q: Which pair of phrases is used to respond to complaints?
o: I'm terribly sorry. / I can only apologise.
It's most disappointing. / I'm not very happy about it.
It's not up to standard. / I've got a complaint.
I want my money. / This is terrible.
mcq.why: These phrases apologise to the customer.

o: The founder of Selfridge's, who coined 'The customer is always right'
mcq.why: He started the store and the famous phrase.

mcq.q: Why do companies use the phrase 'The customer is always right'?
o: To convince customers they will get good service and to encourage staff to give it

mcq.q: Your meal in a restaurant is cold. Which is the best polite complaint?
o: I'm not very happy about my meal; it's cold.
I can only apologise for my meal.
mcq.why: This is a clear, polite complaint.

mcq.q: A customer says the soup is wrong. What could a waiter say to avoid a scene?
o: I'm sorry, let me fix that for you.
It's just not up to standard.
I've got a complaint about you.
mcq.why: An apology and an offer to help calms the customer.

mcq.q: Your tour group's bus breaks down. Which phrase introduces a hypothetical solution?
o: I think I would call another bus company.
I've got a complaint about the bus.
mcq.why: 'I think I would...' suggests an imagined solution.

mcq.q: Why is the guest especially unhappy with this hotel?
o: It is supposed to be five-star but it is more like two-star
It is far from the airport
He does not like the receptionist's name
mcq.why: His expectations of a five-star hotel were not met.

mcq.q: What is one criticism of 'The customer is always right'?
o: It can make employees unhappy when the customer is not right or is rude
It means shops never sell anything
It is too difficult to remember
mcq.why: Customers are not always right, and staff may suffer.

mcq.q: Why does the receptionist call the maintenance department and not room service about the air conditioning?
o: Maintenance repairs equipment; room service brings food
The guest asked for room service
mcq.why: Each department has its own job.
